messages.content: i'm on the free plan and my crawl calls start failing with 429 after just a couple of requests in a minute. is something broken?

Nothing is broken. That 429 is the rate limit. On the Free plan, /crawl allows 2 requests per minute, while /scrape, /map and /search allow 10 per minute. Limits are applied per team, so every API key on your team shares the same counters. If you need more headroom, the Hobby plan raises /crawl to 20 requests per minute.
Do unused credits carry over to next month? We barely used our allotment this cycle.

By default, no: plan credits reset at the start of each monthly cycle and unused ones do not roll over. There are two exceptions. Annual Scale plans roll unused plan credits over 1 month, and annual Enterprise plans roll them over 2 months. Credits you buy yourself are separate and stay on your account until you use them, unless you cancel your subscription.
A bunch of the URLs in my batch came back as 404s. Am I still being charged for those?

Yes. If Firecrawl returned a document, the page costs 1 credit, and that includes pages where the target site answered with an error status such as 403 or 404. Check the metadata.statusCode field in each response so you can stop retrying URLs that are consistently blocked or missing. A scrape that fails outright, where Firecrawl returns no document at all, costs 0 credits.
how many credits does it cost per page if I use JSON extraction and turn on zero data retention at the same time?

Those options stack on top of the base scrape cost. The base scrape is 1 credit per page, JSON format adds 4 credits per page, and Zero Data Retention adds 1 credit per page, so each page costs 6 credits. The same modifiers apply when you use Crawl or Search, since they scrape each page internally.
Our webhook endpoint is sometimes slow. How long does Firecrawl wait, and what happens if we miss one?

Your endpoint must respond with a 2xx status within 10 seconds. If delivery fails because of a timeout, a non-2xx response or a network error, Firecrawl retries automatically: the first retry comes after 1 minute, the second after 5 minutes and the third after 15 minutes. After 3 failed retries the webhook is marked as failed and no further attempts are made.
How can I be sure the webhook calls hitting my server are really from Firecrawl and not someone spoofing them?

Check the HMAC-SHA256 signature on every request. Each webhook includes an X-Firecrawl-Signature header in the form sha256=<hash>. Take the raw request body before parsing it, compute an HMAC-SHA256 with your webhook secret, and compare it to the hash using a timing-safe function such as hmac.compare_digest() in Python or crypto.timingSafeEqual() in Node.js. Reject anything that fails with a 401. Your secret is in the Advanced tab of your account settings, and you should regenerate it right away if you think it has leaked.
We have one API key used by an intern's side project and I don't want it draining the whole team balance. Can I cap just that key?

Yes, you can set a spend limit on that single key. Open the API keys page in the dashboard, open the menu on the key, and click Set limit. Enter a credit limit and choose per day, per week or per month, then click Save. The cap applies to that key alone, whatever your team balance is. Note that the limit is a number of credits, not an amount of money. The key owner or a team admin can set it, and Remove limit clears it.
I set my monthly pay-as-you-go limit to $22. How much will it actually let you charge me?

The limit rounds down to whole 5 USD increments, so a 22 USD limit works as 20 USD, which allows four increments per month. Credits you buy manually with Load more credits do not count toward this limit. If you want five increments, set the limit to 25 USD.
We're giving an API key to an automated agent. Is there a way to make sure it can only ever get markdown back, never raw HTML?

Yes, that is what Key Restrictions are for. You can give a key an allowed-formats list (for example only markdown) and an allowed-endpoints list. They are enforced server-side, so a request cannot override them, and a request for a format that is not on the list is rejected with a 403. Key Restrictions are an enterprise feature, so your Firecrawl account team needs to enable them for your organization first. After that, a team admin sets them from the API Keys page by choosing Restrictions in the key's menu, and changes take effect within about a minute.
If I downgrade from Standard to Hobby today, do I lose my Standard limits right away? And do I get anything back for the rest of the month?

No, a downgrade is scheduled for your next renewal date. Until then you keep your current plan's credits and limits. Unused time on your current plan is not credited or refunded. You can also undo the scheduled downgrade from your billing settings any time before it takes effect.
